Did you actually read the post?

I was being very specific, and though my writing can always be more succinct, those specific points are important distinctions. Again, it may not resonate with you and that’s fine, but it’s helpful for others.
Do you think it isn’t sometimes helpful for people to be called out to do some self-reflection?

Fair enough 🤷‍♂️ but all self improvement stuff is freely available online and is ‘obvious’ to anyone who’s got it figured out. None of it is ever really secret yet many people find it useful. If it was so self-evident and easy then people would just do it.

If it seems like cheap self help to you then you probably are one of the ones who has it figured out. That’s great, I’m glad for you.
Sure! I hope it helps.
Glad it resonates with you. It’s me too!
That is a humbling reaction, thank you. If it helps, then that’s what matters.
👌 think whatever you want dude
Looks like something out of Dark Souls.

items.title: Struggling to nail down the look of portable AI systems for my sci-fi/post-apocalyptic world, Esotera & could use feedback. The key points I'm trying to hit: 1. Unique and immediately recognizable, 2. Cool-looking, 3. Makes sense within the world.
items.text: Struggling to nail down the look of portable AI systems for my sci-fi/post-apocalyptic world, Esotera & could use feedback. The key points I'm trying to hit: 1. Unique and immediately recognizable, 2. Cool-looking, 3. Makes sense within the world.

For context, you can learn more about the Esotera world at www.totalstoryteller.com/esotera. (And shameless self promo for a second, if you want to join the Esotera community (post-apocalyptic media & news, plus Esotera content), go here: https://totalstoryteller.us14.list-manage.com/subscribe?u=d296c41ad663eeb33d486e46d&id=ebcb837e15)

Anyway, this portable AI system is an integral part of the world, and this is the first time we are exploring it. The reason the visuals for this are so important is that Esotera is purely in a film medium right now and I am getting ready to shoot a short film where this AI plays a big role. We will have to create 2 of these portable AI as props for the main character.

I have more brainstorming/world-building sketches of my own (not by Travis Wright) and funnily enough, I'm less concerned about how the AI will function - I feel like I have that figured out pretty well. It's an identifiable, 'iconic' look that I'm trying to find - and that's tough to do.

FYI, the AI in this world range from lacking personality (older models, and those intended for the military, very robotic and matter-of-fact) to more advanced models with a personality mapped onto them and able to do more free-thinking, but they come with some behavioral quirks as a side-effect. This film will have one of each of those types. They will have to look similiar so the audience can still tell what they are by looking at either one.

A friend of mine thinks I need to start with something that looks 'cool' and work backwards to the practical explanation. I've been working the other way around.

Any feedback is very much welcome and appreciated.

More info that might be helpful to know:

Other elements that were important to me for the AI included:
1. Portability
2. Points of attachment (can be carried, attached to vehicle, mounted in various locations, etc.)
3. Universal inputs
4. Modular
5. Strong cooling system
6. Very basic interface (most interfacing done via voice)
7. Slot for the universal Battery+ (a special battery tech in Esotera)
8. Relatively ruggedized, with some models being more rugged than others.

Interesting, what makes you like 6 so much?
That is a pretty interesting idea but probably just not practical for filming purposes for me.

I really appreciate your thoughts - seriously - and I actually was heading in the direction you mentioned. They have a sort of artificial brain (able to form new inter-connections being the key element leading to flexibility and true learning) but capabilities can be expanded by adding hardware upgrade cards for example.

What you said about a window looking into what the ‘brain’ looks like is what I was thinking would look unique and make sense.

I’ll add that the idea of the base material or make of the flexible artificial brain making a difference in quality and capability is interesting. Older models having been created when techniques were more rudimentary and got less bang for the buck.

“You think I’m some water-soft fool who knows not how to spell the name of our own people?”

Lol. These guys were inspired by Fremen, and so because they are literally escaped slaves I called them freemen at first - which is a term for escaped slave. I’ll probably be changing the name though. Too similar.

> It should look like you could drop it down the stairs, to again inform the audience that this isn't space opera but a clumsier, dirtier world.

Thanks for your note - you make a good point that making it this sort of clumsy, heavy duty thing, that feels like you could drop it down stairs and it'd be fine - would say something about the world. Like you said.
The wearable part is a good note. That's the direction I wanted to go initially - something designed to attach to a vehicle or go onto a backpack, which is more like the first few designs.
What about it do you like?
haha I'm the op, I appreciate your input FYI
If it's being worn on a backpack and you're talking to it.

Hahaha that blocky thing from Interstellar? It IS ridiculous, though it is pretty memorable in a way.

Good note about humanizing the machine. That's good feedback. Even HAL-3000 had an eye.

Thanks for your thoughts! FYI - the smiley and vague human face weren't really there for any reason than to show that it's a screen. The AI could be very expressive using the screen, potentially, at least when it's seen.

The reason I'd like to pick a base design to work with is that I'd like the devices to be visually distinct - once you've seen a model once, you can tell pretty much right away, no matter the context, what you're looking at.

And it's a visual icon that viewers can hook onto.
Lol it’s totally cool! It just means you like Dune a lot, which is good in my book. ;)
